notes: Overview: Stonehaven is a payments risk & personalization platform evaluating Dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive inference across US + EU. Primary ask: predictable throughput with cross-region failover and contractual SLOs.
Business driver: reduce decision latency for fraud checks (pre-authorization) and personalized offers at checkout. Cost vs latency tradeoff is critical — CFO wants predictable reserved spend.

Workload profile: mix of short chat-like requests (<=512 tokens) for personalization and very short inference (<=64 tokens) for fraud/reranking. Peaks correlate with US/EU business hours; multi-region footprint required.
Throughput targets: baseline 2k QPS for small (<=64 token) requests globally; burst up to 5k QPS for Black Friday style events. Require per-region throughput guarantees and headroom for failover.

Latency SLOs: p95 < 40ms (short requests), p99 < 120ms hard requirement for payment-decision path. 95/50ms targets for personalized chat acceptable. Any SLA must include tail percentile definitions and measurement method.

Reserved GPU planning ask: initial reserved pool proposal from Redwood - us-east-1: 16 x A100-equivalent; eu-west-1: 8 x A100-equivalent; reserve 25% warm failover capacity cross-region. Customer requests mapping to logical pools by service (fraud vs personalization).

Failover/headroom requirements: want >=20% spare headroom within region for autoscale buffer; cross-region warm standby (cold start avoided) — proposal: maintain minimal warm instances in backup region and route with DNS + regional routing policy.

Kernel/model constraints: running quantized Llama-variant for personalization and a small Transformer classifier for fraud; prefer NVIDIA MIG or partitioning for multi-tenancy. Redwood notes: recommend mixed-size instance pools and per-model batching profiles.

POC summary (2026-02-21): ran 4-hour load test with 3k concurrent short streams from us-east-1 and eu-west-1; observed stable p95=32ms, p99=140ms during a synthetic burst — p99 over target by ~20ms on last-mile network.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-22): 'We cannot accept >120ms p99 for auth decisions — any fallback must be deterministic and explainable.'
Security/compliance notes: SSO/SAML required for Console; must support customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed key wrap. Data residency: EU data must stay in eu-west region for retention >30 days.

Cost sensitivity: CFO prefers committed reserved model with stepped growth; wants options for bursting to shared capacity but with billing visibility. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization to reduce VM counts.

SLA negotiation points: definition of measurement windows, remediation credits tied to regional availability and p99 tails, clear failover sequencing (model fallback list), and data handling during failover.
Network/ops constraints: corporate firewall restricts egress to limited CIDR ranges; requires a pre-approved list of Redwood NAT IPs or Transit connectivity. Networking meeting scheduled 2026-03-12.
